COVID BABIES

By: Tarryn Crossman | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Giving birth during COVID-19

Summary:
Hundreds of thousands of people around the world are dying from COVID 19 but the cycle of life does continue and babies must also be born.
But they will be born into a world more uncertain than ever before in our lifetime.

A woman is never as empowered and vulnerable at the same time, as when she gives birth. Bringing new life into the world can be a scary time on any given day, but doing it during a global pandemic is a whole new experience for these covid babies and their mommies.

The moment you fall pregnant most women immediately start thinking about their birth plan, the way they want to bring this tiny new life into the world and who they want by their side when they do that. Just like every other aspect of life since March 2020 what they wanted or envisioned was no longer important, their birth plans were now all largely been determined by COVID-19 protocols

Further information:
Nilett: case study was supposed to have naturally in a hospital, second baby. But because of her fear of not having her birth partners she chose to do a home birth (at a home birth centre) and loved it so much she wished she had done it with her other boy too. Footage is great
Ronelle: Changed to a home birth at the birthing centre because she was scared of covid, landed up staying the night close to the facility, went into labour quickly and her hubby didn't make it. He watched the whole birth on whatsapp, great character and great footage
TShiwela: landed up having a delivery in hospital alone - went through triage etc. No great footage
Tania: Italian women literally escaped Italy to have their baby in CT with her partner. Home birth was the plan, but due to the baby not coming in time she landed up going to a state facility and having natural alone. No Private OB would let her have it naturally. She had no covid test and was not treated as a PUI. She just cruised through with all the other patients. Amazing story of how a hero nurse helped her give birth. no great footage

The moment you fall pregnant most women start thinking about their birth plan, the way they want to bring this tiny new life into the world and who they want by their side when they do that. But Just like every other aspect of life since March 2020 what these woman wanted or envisioned was no longer important, their birth plans were now all largely been determined by COVID-19 protocols

This was Robyn Jansen van Vuuren’s First baby so for her the most important thing was that her husband was there and that they brought their daughter safely into the world together

I was with a gynecologist And she said to me that the only way that my husband could possibly be present was if it's a natural birth and if we both have covid tests prior to the birth to say that we are both negative.
Thought well you know it's very likely that this is not going to go according to plan
really was my worst nightmare to give birth alone. So for myself to be alone but then also the idea of my husband missing the birth of his daughter which is an experience that you can never get back. It just really was one of the things that just scared me completely

Some hospitals or birthing centres are allowing partners to be present for the whole birth, others only for an hour, and some not at all. But across the board all couples giving birth are required to have covid tests at around 38 weeks. All these are elements are now deciding factors in a birth plan

hubby will be able to be there but only for one hour and after that he has to leave and they can only come back when you get discharged no one else will be able to to visit
. So I decided then to actually change my birth plan and instead of birthing at the hospital I decided to birth at the birth house.

The midwives from the centre where Ronel gave birth normally do 30% of their deliveries at the birth house and the rest at a hospital, but since April they are now doing almost 80% at the birth house.

There are certain risks beacsue it isn’t a hospital so if something goes wrong then you still have to transfer to the birth house to the hospital. Then I had to way up the opetion having husband there and family there vs being at the hospitals with all the rules
I decided to go with the birth house

is a doula, which is someone that offers emotional support to a woman while the MIDWIVES she works with offer the medical support during birth. She is also the co-founder of homebirth an online information platform

So before March I would say they was via our humble website or my dealer website. People were there were maybe 1 to 2 queries per week. And then just before lockdown we. You know the average was about six per day

it all happened in quite a blur

midwife checked me and she told me you're already 8 centimeters dilated.
and things just went really fast.
